title: Suspicious Nmap Scan from Internal Critical Asset

    - 22
    - 23
    - 80
    - 443
    - 445
    - 3389
  count: >100
  timeframe: 60s
condition: count > 100 and src_ip|contains('10.0.1.10')
level: critical
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1046/

author: SOC Team

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Generic {
    meta:
        description = "Detects generic Cobalt Strike beacon characteristics"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0154/"
        date = "2026-04-09"
        hash = "a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890a1b2c3d4e5f67890"
    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 2E 74 65 78 74 00 00 00 [1-4] 00 00 00 00 [1-4] 00 00 00 00 [1-4] 43 6F 62 61 6C 74 53 74 72 69 6B 65 } // Common beacon config marker
        $http_get = "GET / HTTP/1.1" fullword ascii
        $http_post = "POST / HTTP/1.1" fullword ascii
        $user_agent = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64; Trident/7.0; rv:11.0) like Gecko" fullword ascii
    condition:
        all of them and filesize < 2MB
}

The incident highlights a gap in internal segmentation and response capabilities for internal threat pivoting.

Replay analysis identified need to block internal pivot point 10.0.1.10. Attempt to block failed due to policy restrictions.
